pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity St Mary's CofE Primary School - British Values – Preparing children for the future
pageCache.text:
British Values – Preparing children for the future
At Trinity St Mary’s CofE Primary School, British Values are lived every day through our school values of Kindness, Unity and Courage. We believe children flourish when they feel known, valued and inspired to make a positive difference in the world around them.
Through our nurturing Christian ethos, we help children become courageous thinkers, kind citizens, respectful learners and responsible leaders who are confident in their own voice and compassionate towards others.
Children at TSM learn to:
From School, Faith and Eco Councils to pupil leadership, collective worship and courageous advocacy projects, children are encouraged to understand that their choices matter and that they can make a difference.
As a small, caring and inclusive school community, every child is known, supported and encouraged to flourish academically, emotionally and spiritually.
At TSM, we are proud to nurture future citizens who are curious, compassionate and ready to contribute positively to the wider world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity St Mary's CofE Primary School - Church and RE
pageCache.text:
Church and RE
TSM is a part of the Diocese of Southwark.
The Diocese of Southwark is one of the 42 dioceses of the Church of England, which is how the Anglican (Episcopalian Church) is known in England. We are in the Province of Canterbury and are part of the worldwide Anglican Communion which has nearly 70 million members. The Diocese of Southwark is twinned with three Anglican Dioceses in Zimbabwe. The Croydon Episcopal Area is twinned with Central Zimbabwe Diocese, the Woolwich Area with Manicaland and the Kingston Area with Matabeleland. (Southwark Cathedral is twinned with a fourth - Masvingo and Rochester Diocese is twinned with the fifth – Harare.)
In 2017, the Diocese of Southwark launched the Southwark Vision:
Our vision is founded on mutual commitment from all who make up the Diocesan family to walk together in the pilgrimage of faith, supporting, encouraging and resourcing each other in our common task.
At TSM, we work with the Southwark Diocese Board of Education to ensure that we fulfil our mission of educating the children in the parish and creating a welcoming space for all to grow and learn together.

pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity St Mary's CofE Primary School - Headteacher's Welcome to TSM
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome to TSM
A very warm welcome to Trinity St Mary’s CE Primary School – thank you for taking the time to visit us online.
Choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions you will make as a family. At Trinity St Mary’s (TSM), we are proud to offer a nurturing, ambitious and inclusive school community where every child is known, valued and encouraged to flourish.
For over 165 years, TSM has been at the heart of the Balham community, providing children with a safe, happy and inspiring environment in which to learn and grow. As a small one-form entry school, we are able to build strong relationships with every child and family, creating a genuine sense of belonging and partnership from the very beginning of your child’s journey with us.
At TSM, children are encouraged to become confident learners, compassionate friends and curious thinkers. We combine high academic expectations with a creative and enriching curriculum that inspires children to discover their unique talents and develop a lifelong love of learning. Our dedicated staff team, including specialist teachers and lead practitioners, work tirelessly to ensure that every child feels supported, challenged and celebrated.
Our Christian ethos is woven through all aspects of school life and is reflected in our vision of nurturing minds, filling hearts and flourishing together. Guided by our core values of Kindness, Unity and Courage, we encourage children to care for others, believe in themselves and make a positive difference in the world around them. We are proud to be a fully inclusive school where children and families of all faiths and backgrounds are welcomed and respected.
We are delighted that our February 2024 Ofsted inspection recognised the quality of education and care we provide by awarding the school a good judgement. Our SIAMS inspection also recognised the strength of our distinctive Christian character and collective worship.
Whether you are considering Trinity St Mary’s for your child, are already part of our school family, or are simply finding out more about us, we hope our website gives you a sense of the warmth, joy and community that make TSM such a special place to learn and grow.
The best way to experience our school is to visit us in person. We would be delighted to welcome you for a tour with either myself or our Deputy Headteacher, so you can see our school in action, meet our wonderful children and experience the caring atmosphere that sits at the heart of everything we do.
If you would like to arrange a visit or have any questions about admissions, please contact our school office — we are always happy to help.
We look forward to welcoming you and your family to Trinity St Mary’s.
Lynn Anderson Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Worship & Spirtuality
At Trinity St Mary’s, Collective Worship is at the heart of our school community and is an expression of our school's Christian distinctiveness in line with. It is a special time each day when children and staff come together to reflect, pray, sing, celebrate and grow in faith and understanding and follows the guidance set out by the SDBE and Church of England.
“Collective worship is distinctly Christian and absolutely central to the life of the school. Pupils of all denominations, faith and no faith, including the very youngest, find worship meaningful, interesting and enjoyable.” SIAMS Inspection, 2017
Our worship reflects the Christian vision and values of our school while warmly welcoming children and families of all faiths and backgrounds. We aim to create a calm, inclusive and inspiring environment where every child feels valued and encouraged to reflect on life, faith, kindness and the world around them.
Collective Worship provides children with opportunities to:
Each worship begins with a familiar liturgy which helps create a sense of reverence and shared purpose across the school.
A child is chosen to light the candle, marking the beginning of our special “Holy Time” together.
The worship leader says:
“Christ, the light of the world, is here.”
The children respond:
“Lord Jesus shine on us.”
This shared moment helps children pause from the busyness of the day and enter a calm space for reflection and worship.

Our Weekly Collective Worship
Every morning, the whole school gathers for Collective Worship. Each day has a different focus to help children experience worship in a variety of meaningful ways.
Children begin the week by coming together to sing hymns and uplifting songs. Music plays an important role in helping children express joy, gratitude and reflection while strengthening our sense of community.
We celebrate children’s achievements, effort and positive choices through our Merit Worship. Pupils are recognised for demonstrating our school values, showing kindness, perseverance or inspiring others.
This is a joyful opportunity for the school community to encourage and celebrate one another.
Children reflect on the school value for the half-term and consider how they can live out that value in their everyday lives.
Themes such as compassion, courage, friendship, forgiveness and respect help children develop strong moral foundations and thoughtful character.
Our Thursday worship takes place in church and is led by Father Jonathan. This special service includes:
Children enjoy taking an active role and developing confidence in leading worship.
On Fridays, children complete “Deep Thinker” reflections linked to either the previous day’s church worship or the values worship. These activities encourage pupils to think deeply about faith, values and how Christian teachings can connect to their own lives and experiences.
Our Collective Worship themes are carefully planned throughout the year and linked to the Church calendar and Bible teachings.
These themes help children build a growing understanding of Christian faith, teachings and traditions in an engaging and age-appropriate way.

pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity St Mary's CofE Primary School - Faith Council
pageCache.text:
Faith Council
At Trinity St Mary’s CofE Primary School, our Faith Council plays a valuable role in supporting and strengthening the Christian life of our school community and our close partnership with St Mary’s Church, Balham.
The Faith Council provides children with opportunities to develop leadership, reflect on our Christian values and help shape collective worship and spiritual life across the school. Members work closely with staff and the church community to support worship, prayer, reflection and special events throughout the year.
Through links with St Mary’s Church, children are encouraged to deepen their understanding of faith, compassion, service and community. The Faith Council helps to promote our values of Kindness, Unity and Courage while encouraging children to become thoughtful, respectful and courageous advocates who can make a positive difference in the world around them.
Members of the Faith Council also support charitable initiatives, reflection opportunities and acts of service within both the school and wider community, helping all children understand the importance of care, inclusion and belonging.
At TSM, we believe every child can flourish spiritually, emotionally and socially within our nurturing Christian community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity St Mary's CofE Primary School - St Mary's and John the Divine Church
pageCache.text:
St Mary's and John the Divine Church
TSM and our local church have an extremely close relationship. Children from our school visit the church every Thursday as well as visiting during RE lessons and other special occasions.
Our school was pleased to welcome Father Jonathan MacNeaney, who became the vicar at St Mary's & St John The Divine church in September 2023. He has become an integral 'cog' within our school community, continuing the hard work within the school and parish to further develop the wonderful links we have today and continue to support the school with it's Christian identity and role within the community of Balham.
Alongside Father Jonathan, we are very lucky to have such a dedicated team at the church who understand the importance of the school and the Church's role in ensuring all children receive an education that fosters morals and a tolerance of all religions.
Please see the church's website for up-to-date events and news from the parish.
https://www.stmarybalham.org.uk/

pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity St Mary's CofE Primary School - Computing Club Gets Creative with Robotics
pageCache.text:
Computing Club Gets Creative with Robotics
Please enter an introduction for your news story here.
Our Computing Club pupils have been busy developing their problem-solving and teamwork skills through a series of exciting robotics challenges! Using construction and coding kits, the children worked collaboratively to design and build a range of moving models and mechanical creations.
Throughout the sessions, pupils demonstrated fantastic resilience, creativity and communication as they followed instructions, tested ideas and adapted their designs. It was wonderful to see the children supporting one another and sharing their knowledge while exploring how technology and engineering work together.
The club provides an excellent opportunity for children to build confidence in computing while developing important skills such as logical thinking, perseverance and collaboration. The enthusiasm and concentration shown by all the pupils has been outstanding, and we are incredibly proud of their achievements.
We look forward to seeing what our talented young engineers create next!

pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity St Mary's CofE Primary School - KS2 Sleepover Fundraiser
pageCache.text:
KS2 Sleepover Fundraiser
We are excited to announce that our Faith, Eco and School Councils are organising a KS2 Sleepover Fundraiser to raise money for both Shelter and our school.
The sleepover will take place on Friday 19th June from 6:00pm until Saturday 20th June at 8:30am in the school hall.
During the evening, children will enjoy: Pizza and a drink A movie night Games and activities Sleeping in the hall with their friends.
Children must raise a minimum of £10 sponsorship. All money raised will support the work of Shelter as well as projects within our school community.
If you would like to support our children with this charity fundraiser, please contact the school to make a donation.
We hope this will be a memorable evening of friendship, fun and fundraising, and we thank you for your continued support.
